homes.name: A little coffee moment
steps: Put a small spoonful of dry coffee grounds in a cup.
Keep it separate from the other references and notice the aroma from a comfortable distance.
Think of it as the roasted part of your memory, rather than the whole scene.
homes.note: A familiar material reference, not a molecularly validated substitute.

homes.name: A soft vanilla reference
steps: Put a drop of food vanilla extract on a separate paper strip.
Let the alcohol evaporate before checking the scent at a comfortable distance.
Compare its sweet character with your memory; skip it if it feels too dessert-like.
homes.note: An optional scent reference. Do not apply the strip or extract to your skin.

homes.name: A bright citrus opening
steps: Place a small piece of fresh citrus peel in its own dish.
Gently bend the peel away from your face, then leave it in the dish.
Notice whether this is the bright, fresh part you remember.
homes.note: Use the fruit peel as it is; no extraction, heating, or essential oils.

homes.name: A green, fresh accent
homes.item: Fresh mint or basil, if available
steps: Place one fresh herb leaf on a separate dish.
Gently rub it between your fingers and set it down.
Compare the green or minty impression with the memory.
homes.note: Skip any material you are sensitive to. A fresh leaf is a mixture, not a model-tested molecule.

homes.name: A familiar floral reference
homes.item: A familiar rose or jasmine flower you already have
steps: Keep a familiar fragrant flower in a small vase.
Experience its scent naturally without pressing it against your face.
Notice whether the floral character belongs in the memory or feels too strong.
homes.note: No flower available? Skip this part—there is no need to purchase one.

homes.name: The quiet woody detail
homes.item: A clean, familiar unfinished wooden object
steps: Choose a familiar clean wooden object, only if it already has a noticeable natural scent.
Leave it separate from the other references. Do not sand, burn, or heat it.
Use it as a reminder of the scene, rather than an exact woody accord.
homes.note: Do not smell treated wood, furniture coatings, mold, or dusty objects.

homes.name: A gentle tea reference
homes.item: Dry tea leaves you already own
steps: Place a little dry tea in a separate cup.
Notice it at a comfortable distance without inhaling loose particles.
Compare its leafy, dry character with the scene you remember.
homes.note: This evokes one aspect of the memory; it does not reproduce rain, soil, or mustiness.

perfumes.name: Coffee Break
perfumes.difference: Includes lavender and mint; it may feel softer and more aromatic than literal brewed coffee.

perfumes.name: By the Fireplace
perfumes.difference: Smoke and chestnut are central; it may be much sweeter or smokier than the memory.

perfumes.name: When the Rain Stops
perfumes.difference: An aquatic floral interpretation, not a recreation of wet soil or true petrichor.

perfumes.name: Philosykos
perfumes.difference: A fig-tree interpretation; it may add milky fruit that was absent from your memory.

perfumes.name: Eau Rose
perfumes.difference: A rose-focused fragrance with a fruity detail, rather than a complete garden scene.

perfumes.name: Olène
perfumes.difference: A full white-flower bouquet; it will not supply the coffee or woody parts of a memory.

perfumes.name: Wood Sage & Sea Salt
perfumes.difference: A mineral, herbal interpretation; sea salt is a fragrance note, not a claim about a smell-producing salt molecule.
